Country.evidence_source: The remaining four items were added based on QQ features, the most typical adolescent QQ behaviors reported by China Internet Network Information Center (2016), and the concept of interpersonal sexual objectification.

Survey method.evidence_source: OISO experiences were measured using six items. Two were derived from an item from the Interpersonal Sexual Objectification Scale (Kozee et al., 2007): the original item, "How often have you felt like or known that someone was evaluating your physical appearance?", was changed to "How often have you noticed someone evaluating your size or appearance in your photo album on Q-zone?" and "How often have you noticed someone evaluating your size or appearance during QQ communication?".

Assessment of BA.evidence_source: The section describes the measurement of 'Online interpersonal sexual objectification (OISO) experiences' using adapted items, not Body Appreciation (BA).

Number of studies.evidence_source: The text describes the development and psychometric properties of a single measure within what appears to be one study.

section_summary.extract_value: This section details the measurement of Online Interpersonal Sexual Objectification (OISO) experiences. It describes the development of six items, two adapted from the Interpersonal Sexual Objectification Scale and four new items based on QQ features and adolescent behaviors in China. The section also reports psychometric properties including Cronbach's α (0.82), results from Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) yielding a single factor, and Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) indicating adequate model fit.
